item.title: Chichibu Night Festival: One of Japan's Three Great Float Festivals — Guide
item.description: The Chichibu Night Festival, held each December, is ranked among Japan’s three great float festivals and designated a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. Six enormous, elaborately decorated floats — some weighing several tonnes and adorned with intricate wood carvings, lanterns and tapestries — are hauled through the streets by teams of local residents, accompanied by traditional flute and drum music, while a spectacular fireworks display lights the winter sky above. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Chichibu, Saitama Hours Evening, December 2–3 each year Admission Free to view Time needed 3–5 hours (evening parade + fireworks) Best time December 3 evening (main event) What to See Six enormous decorated floats, some weighing several tonnes.

item.title: Kawagoe Festival: A UNESCO-Listed October Float Procession — Guide
item.description: The Kawagoe Festival, held each October and designated a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, transforms Kawagoe’s historic Kurazukuri storehouse street into a stage for towering, elaborately carved floats (dashi), some dating back centuries and adorned with mechanical dolls, lanterns and tapestries. As floats pass one another in the narrow streets, musicians aboard sometimes engage in playful ‘hikkawase’ battles, competing to outplay each other’s traditional flute and drum music in a lively display of local pride.

item.title: Hachinohe Sansha Taisai: UNESCO Float Festival — Guide
item.description: The Hachinohe Sansha Taisai is a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage festival held over five days in late July–early August. A grand procession of 27 towering, elaborately decorated floats bearing mythological tableaux rolls through the city, uniting three major Hachinohe shrines in a 290-year tradition of music, costume and pageantry. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Hachinohe, Aomori Hours Late Jul–early Aug (~Jul 31–Aug 4) Admission Free to watch; some paid seats Time needed 2–3 hours Best time Late July (annual) Highlights 27 towering decorated floats with mythological scenes.
